headline: P0155 (Family Practice, GA): elevated 99215 share, but documentation review largely supports billed 99215s; pattern leans toward a complex panel with a few low-complexity outliers to check
rationale: P0155 bills 99215 on 15.2% of 310 claims versus 4.3% expected for its patient complexity (risk-adjusted score 3.48, peer z 1.48). The excess is concentrated in sicker patients: 99215 share is 18.4-58.3% for patients with 2 to 5+ chronic conditions (vs 5.6-29.8% for all providers), while patients with 0-1 conditions are only modestly above peers (5.0% vs 2.1%, 4.8% vs 3.4%; 6 claims total). The documentation review is the key evidence: of 16 documented 99215 claims, only 2 (12.5%) were unsupported (C0071491, C0071536, both documented moderate MDM), about half the all-provider rate of 24.2%, and examples such as C0071524, C0071612, C0071623 and C0071629 show high MDM with 45-51 minutes. Unsupported rates at 99213 (3.8%) and 99214 (8.7%) are at or below peers. Overall this is consistent with a legitimately complex panel billed at higher intensity rather than systematic upcoding, though 16 documented 99215s is a modest sample and the provider still bills 99215 more often than peers even within complexity strata. A few 99215s on low-complexity patients with single simple diagnoses (e.g., C0071404 low back pain, C0071411 UTI, C0071429 hypertension only) merit spot review.
next_steps: Pull records for the 99215 claims on 0-1 condition patients (C0071404, C0071411, C0071412, C0071429, C0071579, C0071599) to confirm high MDM or qualifying time.
Expand documentation sampling of 99215 claims beyond the 16 reviewed to confirm the low unsupported rate holds.
Review C0071491 and C0071536 (documented moderate MDM) to determine whether they reflect isolated coding errors or a time-based billing misunderstanding.
Compare within-stratum 99215 rates for 2-3 condition patients against same-specialty peers in GA to see whether the residual excess is explained by panel acuity not captured by condition counts.
If expanded review stays near or below the all-provider unsupported rate, consider closing with provider education rather than escalation.
